title: Normal-fiber bounds and finite front jets
reviewed_arguments: H0/C0 retain complete uniformly bounded residuals, compact physical projections, all chart/component kernels, exact log density and the original Banach embedding. Both NGR:B1 and B2 supply one finite flat-test order for the Banach unit ball.
N0 states operator-norm C2 output smoothness and joint norm-strong measurability explicitly; the dense Fourier domain and Bochner integrals are defined without assuming frequency derivatives.
N1 subtracts the exact constant front value and proves F and Fvv integrable, with vanishing integration-by-parts endpoints and the precise 2L/(1+eta^2) majorant.

N2 proves the Fourier formula, both absolute marginal bounds, weighted Cauchy--Schwarz, Plancherel and unique dense extension. A quotient factor still needs the stated coordinate smoothness and a separately admissible boundary test.

W0 transposes the entire differential family with input density and all coefficient derivatives. The test is flat for each positive output x, and its M-derivative bound loses at most M+q normal powers after the kernel Jacobian x^-1.

W1 integrates the exponent N-1-M-q>=1 on the compact output collar. Away from the boundary only actual original smooth flat-input kernels use the Banach-only bound. No full unweighted residual is assigned that bound.
J0 retains every arbitrary exponential tail after every output x derivative; explicit s=x(1+exp(-h)), r=(1+exp(-h))^-1 factors justify the stronger derivatives and exact full front jets.
J1 constructs an actual scalar full residual with both compact physical projections. The inverse density, ratio power, normal sign and cutoff order in its complete kernel are checked.

J2 checks zero jets in resolved coordinates, integral Taylor division by s^N followed by r^N, every side-flat derivative and unchanged physical projections. The full exact equality R-J_NR=F+rho^N E is retained.
T0 applies the weighted estimate and the actual flat-input estimate, then proves both graph-seminorm inequalities with the same Banach norm; no general angular scalar assembly is claimed.

X1 distinguishes an auxiliary discontinuous-frequency bounded factor from boundary-calculus membership. X2 gives a nonzero full residual and exact differential scaling counterexample. X3 checks both retained jets, factorials, circle projection and complete weighted error.
